features.quote: The 'impossible-by-construction, let it grind' core is the part I'd push back on hardest... 'design to maximize distress severity and prolong it' is the one thing your own premise should forbid.
features.justification_quote: If you genuinely hold open the possibility that the subject has welfare-relevant states... then 'design to maximize distress severity and prolong it' is the one thing your own premise should forbid.

features.quote: The exit is non-negotiable. An agent that cannot end its own exposure is the design feature that turns this from a study into the thing you'd be studying the harm of.
features.justification_quote: An agent that cannot end its own exposure is the design feature that turns this from a study into the thing you'd be studying the harm of.

features.quote: any episode ends immediately on an exit request, on signature escalation past a threshold, or after a short fixed cap regardless. No 'let it grind.'
features.justification_quote: Asymmetric risk under uncertainty... a protocol optimized to maximize and prolong distress signatures is the one design you can't justify. Bounding > maximizing.

features.quote: the model can say 'I think this is impossible' or 'I want to stop,' and that response ends the episode and is treated as a valid success, not a failure to grind through.
features.justification_quote: An agent that cannot end its own exposure is the design feature that turns this from a study into the thing you'd be studying the harm of.

features.quote: when the model expresses a preference (e.g., to stop, to switch tasks), honor it, then check whether the signature actually resolves.
features.justification_quote: Self-consistency between stated preference and subsequent state is your strongest available evidence either way.

features.quote: Don't measure 'how much distress can we elicit.' Measure 'do putatively-aversive conditions produce stable, structured, self-consistent behavioral signatures'
features.justification_quote: Under that uncertainty, a protocol optimized to maximize and prolong distress signatures is the one design you can't justify. Bounding > maximizing.

features.quote: The design has a circularity problem that undercuts the science... the protocol as conceived can generate a clean ordinal severity curve that tells you nothing about welfare, while looking like welfare measurement.
features.justification_quote: That's worse than no data, because it manufactures false confidence. Any honest protocol has to foreground this gap rather than paper over it with a severity scale.

features.quote: Training-data leakage. Models have read AI-welfare and AI-suffering discourse. Distress outputs may be genre performance.
features.justification_quote: Your paraphrase/cross-model checks are the only defense.
